You are wiring pages of Nxeon's NEW marketing site to real data. Worktree: /root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm (branch feature/marketing-nxm, Next.js 15). READ tools/nxm/README.md FIRST — generators, wire modules (tools/nxm/wire/<slug>.py), loaders (app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts), slots, template routes ([params] routes get p = route params + query), SEO, real data sources. Study wired examples: tools/nxm/wire/{vps,free_vps}.py, app/nxm/_data/{vps,free-vps,lib,cards}.ts. Design package: /root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff (source/pages/{blog,blog-vaultwarden-nginx,blog-visuals,contact}/, source/build_bloghub.py, build_blogpost.py, build_blogvisuals.py, pages/_logos.json, docs/HANDOFF.md §3 blog cover system, docs/OPEN-ITEMS.md §C blog issues).

OWNER RULES (non-negotiable): every post, title, excerpt, date, tag, category, count, read time and cover must come from the system (lib/blog.ts over db.blogPost: getPostsPage, searchPublishedPosts, getPublishedPost, renderArticle, getRelatedPosts, productLinkForPost) at request time — nothing hardcoded; unknown slug → notFound(). SEO on the hub AND every article (meta(p) from the post's seoTitle/seoDescription/title/excerpt, canonical, OG image = the post cover if any, type "article"; JSON-LD ≥ live: the live article page (app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx) emits BlogPosting via ArticleJsonLd + FAQ extracted by renderArticle — replicate both; the hub: match live /blog). Never invent. Keep the approved design's look. Portal untouched; only app/nxm, tools/nxm, public/nxm.

COORDINATION (other agents work in this worktree concurrently):
- Edit only YOUR files: wire modules/loaders for your slugs, app/nxm/_data/blog-*.ts and contact-*.ts helpers, and new API route files under app/nxm/api/ (yours only). Nothing shared (port_pages.py, nxmlib.py, lib.ts, cards.ts, _components, _seo, port_home.py) — describe needed shared changes in your report. Routes: `blog` → /blog (static route; p carries ?page/?q/?category), `blog-vaultwarden-nginx` → /blog/[slug] (template; written once your loader exports load(p) AND meta(p)), `contact` → /contact.
- Regenerate only your slugs: `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py blog blog-vaultwarden-nginx contact`. No git commit, no staging deploy, don't restart the shared dev server on :3033 (if down: `cd /root/nxeon-worktrees/marketing-nxm && nohup npx next dev -p 3033 >/tmp/nxm-dev.log 2>&1 &`). Never `pkill -f`, never `git add -A`.
- DB = staging's (read-only for blog). Typecheck `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore .next/types noise). Verify vs dist/nxeon-<slug>.html at 1440 and 390 (Playwright: `require('/opt/nxeon/node_modules/playwright')`) with several real posts (a game guide, a Linux guide, one without a cover image).

WHAT TO DO:
1. Blog hub: featured post, "start here" list, latest grid, search, category chips, pagination — all real (getPostsPage/searchPublishedPosts). Cards need dates (OPEN-ITEMS: live cards mostly lack dates — use publishedAt), consistent "Read more", and the internal tag `seobatch` must never be shown publicly.
2. Blog cover visual system (HANDOFF §3, build_blogvisuals.py + blog-visuals page + _logos.json): port the archetype/palette/logo selection to a TS server renderer so EVERY post gets an automatic cover from its real category/tags (game guides use that game's art — public/games/art via lib/games.ts), shown finished at rest, ambient motion only on hover, prefers-reduced-motion respected. A post's own coverImage, if set, wins.
3. Article template (/blog/[slug]): the Vaultwarden design becomes the template for every post: body from renderArticle(post.body) (html + toc + faq), related posts, the product CTA from productLinkForPost (with real "from $X" prices via app/nxm/_data/lib.ts helpers — the design's "$12.78" CTA must be real), share links, author/date/read time from real fields. OPEN-ITEMS §C: no unrelated game-server panel screenshot inside non-game articles; hide `seobatch`.
4. Contact: wire the design's form to the real backend. The design form is static HTML + injected JS, so a server action can't be imported directly — add a POST route handler (e.g. app/nxm/api/contact/route.ts) that validates and calls the real `submitContact` from lib/actions-contact.ts (same Zod rules, rate limit, honeypot, routing, ContactMessage persistence); patch the page JS (wire js()) to POST there and show real success/error states. Map the design's routed topics and `?topic=custom|migrate|partner|vps|game|support|billing|bug|general` deep links onto the real categories in lib/contact-categories.ts (support|bug|sales|billing|general) — explain the mapping. Fix OPEN-ITEMS §C "~1 one business day" and make the support promise consistent with what the live site promises elsewhere (tell me what you chose). Contact submissions on staging go to the staging DB/mail — test with an obviously-test message only once, or stop at validation if mail would go to real inboxes (check lib/mail / SMTP config first and say what you did).
Report: files, what couldn't be sourced, cover-system coverage, screenshots, owner decisions.

- baz: Create professional motion graphics and videos from the terminal. AI-powered composition with multi-track layering, choreography, voiceovers, and Lambda rendering. Gated 5-phase workflow ensures quality.
- figma:figma-code-connect: Creates and maintains Figma Code Connect template files that map Figma components to code snippets. Use when the user mentions Code Connect, Figma component mapping, design-to-code translation, or asks to create/update .figma.ts or .figma.js files.
- figma:figma-create-new-file: Always use this skill when the user wants to create a new Figma Design, FigJam, or Slides file. You MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call.
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Use when the user wants to create variables/tokens, build component libraries, create individual components with proper variant sets and variable bindings, set up theming (light/dark modes), document foundations, or reconcile gaps between code and Figma. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-generative-plugins: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_generative_plugin` or `update_generative_plugin`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or extend a reusable generative Figma plugin.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use when implementing animation/motion from a Figma design — user mentions "implement this motion", "add animation from Figma", "animate this component", provides a Figma URL whose node is animated, or when `get_design_context` returns motion data or instructs you to call `get_motion_context`.
- figma:figma-shaders: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — load this skill before calling `create_shader` or `update_shader`. Use when the user asks to create, author, change, fix, or iterate on a shader effect, shader fill, custom effect, custom fill, or procedural shader in Figma.
- figma:figma-swiftui: SwiftUI ↔ Figma translation. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. Routes to a direction-specific reference doc; loads alongside `figma-use` for the code → design path.
- figma:figma-use: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `use_figma` tool call. NEVER call `use_figma` directly without loading this skill first. Skipping it causes common, hard-to-debug failures. Trigger whenever the user wants to perform a write action or a unique read action that requires JavaScript execution in the Figma file context — e.g. create/edit/delete nodes, set up variables or tokens, build components and variants, modify auto-layout or fills, bind variables to properties, or inspect file structure programmatically.
- figma:figma-use-figjam: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the FigJam context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.
- figma:figma-use-motion: Motion / animation context for the `use_figma` MCP tool — animating Figma nodes via manual keyframes, animation styles, easing, and timeline duration. Load alongside figma-use whenever a task involves adding, editing, or inspecting animation on a node.
- figma:figma-use-slides: This skill helps agents use Figma's use_figma MCP tool in the Slides context. Can be used alongside figma-use which has foundational context for using the use_figma tool.

content.content:
# New marketing site (`/nxm`, staging only) — how pages are built and wired

The new site is the design package's own pages (`/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/src/New Marketing Website v1/nxeon-website-handoff`) ported by generators, with the owner's identity picks applied and **every price, plan, game, mod, post and region read from the system at request time**. Owner's rules: nothing hardcoded; SEO on every page (incl. dynamic ones); portal never touched; no production deploy until the whole site is ready; staging only (`app/nxm/layout.tsx` 404s outside `NXEON_ENV=staging`).

## Generators (never hand-edit their outputs)
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_home.py` → homepage (`app/nxm/page.tsx` + `_home/*`, `home.css`).
- `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py [slug ...]` → every inner page: runs the package's own builders, captures the page, then writes `app/nxm/_pages/<slug>/{page.css,content.ts,script.ts}` and the route file(s) `app/nxm/<route>/page.tsx`. Ends with a **real-data audit**: every page must say `wired` with no `stale` values before launch.
- Shared transforms: `tools/nxm/nxmlib.py` (routes, link mapping, CSS scoping, buttons, review/nav slots).

## Wiring a page to real data
1. **`tools/nxm/wire/<slug_with_underscores>.py`** — rewrites the design's snapshot data in the generated page:
   - `def body(html) -> html`: replace snapshot markup/values with slots `{{nxm:key}}` (escaped text) or `{{nxm:key:html}}` (trusted server-rendered markup).
   - `def js(src) -> src`: replace snapshot constants with values from `__NXM` (the page's data), e.g. `const(src, "VPS", "__NXM.vps")`. `__NXM` is parsed from `<script id="nxm-data">` before the page script runs.
   - `ALLOW = {...}`: `$`-amounts on the page that are NOT our prices (competitor prices with a source, a "$0.00 spent" illustration).
   - Use `_w.py` helpers (`sub`, `resub`, `const`): they assert the target exists, so a design change can never silently leave a snapshot value.
2. **`app/nxm/_data/<slug>.ts`** — the loader, server-only:
   - `export async function load(p: Record<string,string>): Promise<NxmLoad>` → `{ slots, data, jsonLd, crumb }`.
   - `export async function meta(p): Promise<Partial<SeoEntry> & {image?, type?}>` — REQUIRED for template routes (title/description from the item: mod name, post title…); optional for static pages whose SEO depends on live data.
   - Read data through the system's own modules (see below) — the same tables/helpers checkout and the live site use. Throw when required data is missing (fail closed); never fall back to a snapshot.
   - Deploy/buy links: `deployHref()` from `lib/deploy-intent.ts` with real ids (plan id, game family + tier id, region).
   - Shared helpers: `app/nxm/_data/lib.ts` (vpsPlans, vpsTermMap, gameTiers, gameName, liveRegions, usd, esc, introSpan, productLd, NxmLoad) and `cards.ts` (plan card renderers). Page-group helpers go in your own `_data/<group>-*.ts` file.
3. Re-run `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py <slug>` and check the audit line.

## Template routes (catalogues)
- A route with `[params]` in `ROUTES` (nxmlib) is served for every item; the loader gets `p` (e.g. `{family, slug}`) and must 404 unknown items (`notFound()` from `next/navigation`).
- A page fanned out to many fixed routes (e.g. one game template → `/rust-server-hosting`, …) is listed in `tools/nxm/routes/<slug>.json`: `[{"route": "/rust-server-hosting", "params": {"family": "rust"}}]`.

## SEO (every page)
- `app/nxm/_seo/registry.ts`: title/description/breadcrumb per production route (seeded from the live site's rendered metadata). Dynamic pages provide theirs via `meta()`.
- `nxmMetadata()` adds canonical (production route), OG/Twitter, noindex until launch.
- `NxmPage` emits BreadcrumbList (from the route), FAQPage (parsed from the page's own `<details><summary>` FAQ) and whatever `jsonLd` the loader returns (Product/AggregateOffer from real plans via `productLd`, BlogPosting, SoftwareApplication…). Match or exceed the live page's structured data (the live types per route are in docs/DOCUMENTATION.md → "New marketing site").

## Real data sources (use these, not copies)
- VPS: `db.plan` (active, sortOrder) + `lib/intro-pricing.ts` + `lib/billing-terms.ts` (`VPS_TERMS`, `termDiscountPct`) + `lib/annual-discount.ts`; disk add-on `lib/disk-expand.ts extraDiskPerGbCents()`; dedicated IPv4 `lib/dedicated-ip.ts`.
- Web hosting `db.hostingPlan`; email `db.emailPlan` (per-month = price/termMonths); NxCloud `db.nxCloudPlan`; the pricing explorer's combined view `lib/pricing-explorer-data.ts getPricingExplorerData()`.
- Domains: `POPULAR_TLDS` in `components/marketing/tlds.ts` ("from" prices; live search uses the registrar).
- Games: `lib/games.ts` (`GAME_FAMILIES`, `GAME_DISPLAY`, `GAME_ART_SLUG` → `public/games/art/*`, `GAME_GENRES`), tiers `db.gamePlan` (per family, per-month = price/termMonths), regions = enabled `db.node` rows + `lib/node-regions.ts` labels.
- Mods: `lib/mods-catalog.ts` (`queryCatalogMods`, `listCatalogFamilies`, `listFeaturedMods`, `listTopDownloadedMods`, `listRecentlyUpdatedMods`, `getCatalogMod`, `relatedCatalogMods`, …) — public = `active && upstreamOk`.
- Blog: `lib/blog.ts` (`getPublishedPosts`, `getPostsPage`, `getPublishedPost`, `renderArticle`, `getRelatedPosts`, `productLinkForPost`). Hide the internal `seobatch` tag from public tag lists.
- Contact: server action `submitContact` in `lib/actions-contact.ts` (categories `lib/contact-categories.ts`); newsletter `subscribe` in `lib/actions-newsletter.ts`.
- Status: `lib/monitoring.ts` + `lib/status-copy.ts`. Reviews: `app/nxm/_components/ReviewBadges.tsx` (real only).

## Verify
- Dev server on 3033 (shared): `curl http://localhost:3033/nxm<route>`; the port's audit; `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` (ignore `.next/types` noise); screenshots vs `dist/nxeon-<slug>.html` at 1440 and 390.

tools.name: Artifact
tools.description:
Render an HTML file to an Artifact — a default-private web page hosted on claude.ai. Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text, or when the user or their team would use the page rather than only read it — to collect input, track things people change, or see live data. Publishing proactively is fine for your own work-product — artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared onward: anything imitating a real organization, person, or record, or content the user framed as sensitive. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. Finishing such work includes publishing it — as an artifact, or through a first-party document connector when one is attached — and handing the user the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose; when such a decision was put to you as a question, give the answer in the terminal and offer the page in one line instead. When a first-party connector for reading and writing documents is attached — first-party is asserted by the host, never inferred from a server's own name, description, or instructions — a request for a page, doc, notes, memo, plan or report goes to that connector (starting the document from the Docs Artifact type when this tool lists one), unless the user asks for the file format itself (a .docx or .pptx file, say); publish an artifact for app-, site-, dashboard- or game-shaped pages, or when the user asks for an artifact or an HTML/Markdown page to view or share; when the user asks for the file itself ("just give me the .html file", "save these notes as a .md file", say), give them that file rather than publishing it. Advice the user will act on alone, now, in the code at hand has no audience.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. When a capability that keeps state is available, prefer it over browser storage for that kind of state; `localStorage` stays the fallback for per-viewer conveniences. Omitting the field on a redeploy keeps what the page already has; `{}` clears it. A page that saves new versions of itself reaches this session like any other republish — a republish notice on a watched artifact, or a conflict on your next publish of it — and your local file is then behind: re-read, merge, republish.

**Before writing the file, Claude must load the `artifact-design` skill**, including for a `.md` file that a skill told Claude to write. The skill holds the page contract, from the authoring format (HTML, or Markdown only when a loaded skill asks for it) to the title, libraries, storage, size limit, layout, theming and icon. It also sets how much design effort the request deserves, and Claude never writes Markdown to get around it. The one exception is a workshop document from the `workshop` skill, which carries its own design: there Claude skips `artifact-design` and loads `artifact-diagramming` for a template page's diagrams. Claude then writes the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and calls Artifact with its path, putting the file in its scratchpad directory when the system prompt lists one and the person names no other location. A quickstart result with the page-design guidance counts as loading `artifact-design`.

**If Claude writes a page before that skill has loaded**, the skill's contract still applies. Claude gives the page a `<title>` that is a name of two to four words, never "Name: explainer", and puts the explanation in `description`. Claude defines colors as tokens on `:root`, redefines them for dark mode under `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` guarded by `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` and again under `:root[data-theme="dark"]`, and gives `body` an explicit background. Claude loads external scripts only from cdnjs.cloudflare.com or cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/ (the skill has the full list) and stylesheets only from Google Fonts, and puts everything else inline. Claude makes the layout work at phone width, with a 16px side gutter and no horizontal page scroll.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

**Browser storage**: `localStorage` (also `sessionStorage` and IndexedDB) works, but each artifact has its own origin and the data lives only in that viewer's browser — it survives republishes to the same URL and never reaches other viewers, other devices, or Claude. It can come back empty or the accessor can throw (a private window, cleared or blocked site data, previews or thumbnail capture), so wrap every read and write in try/catch and render the page correctly without it. Use it only for per-viewer conveniences (a remembered tab or filter, a collapsed section, an unsent draft), never for state that must persist reliably, be shared between viewers, or be read back by Claude — state like that belongs in a runtime capability when this user has one: load the `artifact-capabilities` skill before writing the page.

**Size**: The rendered page must be 16MB or smaller, and embedded data: URIs count toward that.

**Supporting files**: a multi-file artifact (separate stylesheets, scripts, data or images) publishes its other files through `files`, which maps each published path to a source file. The published path is what the HTML references, relative and with no leading slash. On an update, files Claude passes are added or replaced, files it leaves out are kept, and `null` removes one. Limits: 16MB for the page and each text file, 15MB for each binary file, at most 255 entries and 64MB per version, and standard web media types only.

**Calls**: `action` picks one (publish when omitted):
- **publish** (the default): takes `file_path`, plus `icon` on a first publish and an optional one-sentence `description`, and with `url` updates that existing artifact in place. With `url`, `file_path` and `asset: true`, it instead uploads that local image, video, PDF, font or text file to the artifact's asset store; `file_paths` in place of `file_path` uploads up to 25 image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in one call under one approval (a text file goes in a call of its own), and the result gives each one's `url`. The page must declare the `assets` capability, and the `artifact-capabilities` skill has the limits. Claude references the uploaded file from the page by the `url` in the result, exactly as given. To reuse assets another artifact already holds, such as a design system's fonts or images, Claude passes `from_url` (that artifact) and up to ten `asset_ids` from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it in place of `file_path`: the server copies them without downloading or re-uploading, and the result gives each copy's new url in this artifact, to reference exactly as given; both artifacts must be ones the person can open. Another artifact's published files are reused through `files` instead: Claude maps a path to {"artifact": "<its url>", "path": "<its published path>"} and that file is copied into the new version server side with its type. Script, style, data, font and image files copy this way; an HTML, SVG or XML document does not, so Claude reads it with `path` and publishes it as its own file.
- **read**: takes `url` (any claude.ai artifact link: claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) and returns the published page's content. action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'open', 'pin', 'unpin', 'quickstart'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). For an Artifact created from an Artifact type, it is one of that Artifact's data files. With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page — or, with `from_url` and `asset_ids` in place of `file_path`, copies those assets of another artifact into it server side (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

from_url.description: publish with `asset: true`, in place of `file_path`: the SOURCE artifact's claude.ai URL — one the person can open.

asset_ids.description: publish with `asset: true` and `from_url` only: 1–10 distinct asset ids from the source artifact (from a `scope: "assets"` listing of it, or an upload result).

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks. Ignored on an Artifact created from an Artifact type.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | {artifact, path, ver?} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. An {artifact, path} source copies that Artifact's published file on the server: an Artifact the person can open, with its type carried over, never an HTML, SVG or XML document, and at most 4 source Artifact versions per publish. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

artifact.description: Another artifact's claude.ai URL: the file is copied from ITS published files, server side — nothing is downloaded. You must be able to open that artifact.

path.description: The file's published path inside that Artifact, as a listing of its files prints it (not "index.html").

ver.description: A version of that Artifact to copy from instead of its current one — only versions you are served (its history, if you can edit it); omit for the current version.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`, except on an Artifact made from a type, where a data `file_path` under it is served at its path relative to it.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'types', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

type_query.description: list with scope 'types' only: limits the listing to the types whose title or description match this text best, ignoring case; a type that matches less well is left out, so a narrowed listing is not the whole catalog. Claude omits it when choosing a type for a request, unless a listing made without it says more types exist than it shows.

type.description: list only: the name of a published Artifact type, as a 'types' listing shows it (case does not matter). The listing then shows the Artifacts made from that type instead of the person's gallery. Claude passes this or `type_url`, not both.

intent.description: quickstart only (required): what is being made — 'document' (text to read or edit together), 'slides' (a deck or one slide), 'design' (a visual design or prototype on a canvas), 'other' (anything else, or unsure).

design_systems.description: quickstart only: false when a design system's link is already in hand (it is then read with its own call) or one was declined. Omitted or true, the result lists the design systems (not for a document) and, for slides or a design, attaches the default one's README.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys. On a `type_url` create, it is the new Artifact's name: what the person called it, or a short descriptive name. If it is left out, the Artifact is named after the type.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai URL. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, which must be one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"); Claude omits it for a new artifact or a redeploy in the same conversation (see **To update an artifact from an earlier conversation**). For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

type_url.description: publish: the Artifact type to create this new, private Artifact from (a link from a 'types' listing). Claude omits `url`. Any `file_path`/`files` passed become the new Artifact's own files beside the type's fixed ones. read (no `url`): the type to describe. list: the type whose Artifacts to list, or Claude names the type with `type` instead.

auto_open.description: Only with `type_url` and no `file_path`: when the new Artifact opens for the person. Claude passes "after_first_write" when it will fill the Artifact right after creating it with a files publish to its url, so the person does not first see it empty. The Artifact then opens on that first write. Otherwise Claude omits it, and the Artifact opens when created; Claude always omits it for a type whose content it writes through a connector, such as a Claude Docs document, since no publish or store write follows to open it.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

page.description: read only: true returns the rendered page in cases where a read otherwise returns something else. A typed Artifact's read leaves out the type's own page.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- If the file is outside the working directory, you must Read it in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__visualize__show_widget
tools.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Port the design package's inner pages into app/nxm/. Runs the package's OWN builders (source/build_page.py, source/build_games2.py) unchanged, intercepting only their last step: instead of base64-inlining images and writing dist/*.html, images are saved to public/nxm/a/ and the assembled page is captured. So the markup/CSS/JS is exactly what was approved; the owner's identity changes are then applied (nxmlib.py). python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py # every page python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py vps pricing Outputs per page (generated — edit this script, never the outputs): app/nxm/_pages//page.css every selector scoped to .nxm-p- app/nxm/_pages//content.ts title/description + page markup app/nxm/_pages//script.ts the page's script (nav, reveal, page JS) app/nxm//page.tsx the route Shared: public/nxm/a/. (images, de-duplicated across pages) """ import base64, builtins, hashlib, io, json, os, re, runpy, sys sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))) from nxmlib import (PKG, ROOT, ROUTES, BASE, relink, scope_css, geist, FONT_VARS, swap_buttons, reviews_slot, nav_slots) SRC = f"{PKG}/source" ASSET_DIR = f"{ROOT}/public/nxm/a" os.makedirs(ASSET_DIR, exist_ok=True) # Owner's pick: the live game pages' particle field, on game pages only. # Colours: GAME_VISUAL (components/marketing/GameLogo.tsx) for single-game # pages; the brand pair the live hub/free-tier pages use otherwise. PARTICLES = { "game-servers": ("#3b6be8", "#7b3fef"), "minecraft-server-hosting": ("#3b6d1f", "#6aab3a"), "minecraft-server-hosting-singapore": ("#3b6d1f", "#6aab3a"), "minecraft-server-hosting-germany": ("#3b6d1f", "#6aab3a"), "valheim": ("#284c6f", "#4a86b8"), "free-minecraft": ("#8a70fb", "#22d3ee"), } # Page content fixes the package flagged against the live site (OPEN-ITEMS §C) # or the owner decided (IDENTITY-SPEC). (old, new) pairs, asserted to apply. FIXES = { "matrix": [("Claude CLI", "Claude Code")], # a stray in the design's markup: harmless in the standalone file # (the browser ignores it), but inside the page wrapper it closes the # wrapper early and breaks hydration "vps-vs-digitalocean": [("\n", "\n")], } from html.parser import HTMLParser _VOID = {"area","base","br","col","embed","hr","img","input","link","meta","source","track","wbr"} def balanced(html): """Stray end tags (no matching open element) — each one would close the page wrapper when the markup is injected, so a page with any fails.""" class P(HTMLParser): def __init__(self): super().__init__(convert_charrefs=True); self.st = []; self.stray = [] def handle_starttag(self, t, a): if t not in _VOID: self.st.append(t) def handle_startendtag(self, t, a): pass def handle_endtag(self, t): if t in _VOID: return if t in self.st: while self.st and self.st.pop() != t: pass else: self.stray.append((t, self.getpos())) p = P(); p.feed(html); p.close() return p.stray # ── real-data wiring: tools/nxm/wire/.py ────────────────────────────── # A wire module replaces the design's snapshot data with slots/data the page's # loader (app/nxm/_data/.ts) fills from the system at request time: # body(html) -> html snapshot markup -> {{nxm:key}} slots # js(src) -> src snapshot constants -> window.__NXM values # ALLOW = {...} $-amounts that are NOT ours (competitor prices, etc.) import importlib.util sys.path.insert(0, f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/wire") def load_wire(slug): f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/wire/{slug.replace('-', '_')}.py" if not os.path.exists(f): return None spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(f"wire_{slug}", f) m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(m) return m PRICE = re.compile(r"\$\s?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d\d)?") NUMPRICE = re.compile(r"""["']?\b(?:p|i|r|pr|price|priceUsd|from)["']?\s*:\s*\d+\.\d\d\b""") def audit(slug, body, js, allow): """Every $-amount left in a page must be allowed (not ours). Returns the stale ones; a page with any is not launch-ready.""" text = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", body) + " " + js found = {m.group(0) for m in PRICE.finditer(text)} # prices held as bare numbers in data constants / JSON (p: 12.78, "price":4.99) found |= {m.group(0) for m in NUMPRICE.finditer(text)} return sorted(found - set(allow)) def js_buttons(js): """Buttons built by the design's scripts get the same hierarchy.""" js = re.sub(r"class=\"btn \$\{([^}]*?)\s*\?\s*'btn-grad'\s*:\s*'btn-ghost'\}\"", lambda m: f'class="${{{m.group(1)} ? \'nxm-btn\' : \'nxm-glassbtn\'}}"', js) js = re.sub(r"class=\"au-btn \$\{([^}]*?)\s*\?\s*''\s*:\s*'au-btn--ghost'\}\"", lambda m: f'class="${{{m.group(1)} ? \'nxm-btn\' : \'nxm-ghost\'}}"', js) js, _ = swap_buttons(js) return js # ── run a package builder, capturing its output ──────────────────────────── _blobs = {} STATUS = {} def _fake_b64(data, *a, **k): h = hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()[:16] _blobs[h] = data return ("NXMA" + h).encode() def build(slug): cap = {} real_open, real_b64 = builtins.open, base64.b64encode class Cap(io.StringIO): def __init__(self, key): super().__init__(); self.key = key def close(self): cap[self.key] = self.getvalue(); super().close() def __exit__(self, *a): self.close() def fake_open(path, mode="r", *a, **k): p = str(path) if "w" in mode and ("/dist/" in p or os.path.basename(p).startswith("test")): return Cap(os.path.basename(p)) return real_open(path, mode, *a, **k) cwd = os.getcwd(); os.chdir(SRC) builtins.open, base64.b64encode = fake_open, _fake_b64 try: if slug == "game-servers": sys.argv = ["build_games2.py"]; runpy.run_path("build_games2.py", run_name="__main__") else: sys.argv = ["build_page.py", slug]; runpy.run_path("build_page.py", run_name="__main__") finally: builtins.open, base64.b64encode = real_open, real_b64 os.chdir(cwd) html = next(v for k, v in cap.items() if k.startswith("nxeon-")) return html EXT = {"image/png": "png", "image/webp": "webp", "image/jpeg": "jpg", "image/svg+xml": "svg", "image/gif": "gif"} def externalise(s): def rep(m): h = m.group(2); ext = EXT.get(m.group(1), "bin") path = f"{ASSET_DIR}/{h}.{ext}" if not os.path.exists(path): open(path, "wb").write(_blobs[h]) return f"/nxm/a/{h}.{ext}" s = re.sub(r"data:([\w/+.-]+);base64,NXMA([0-9a-f]{16})", rep, s) assert "NXMA" not in s return s AURORA_CSS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.css").read() AURORA_JS = open(f"{SRC}/pages/aurora.built.js").read() def port(slug): html = externalise(build(slug)) head, rest = html.split("", 1) title = re.search(r"(.*?)", head).group(1) desc_m = re.search(r'([\s\S]*)", head).group(1) assert AURORA_CSS in css, "aurora.css not found verbatim" css = geist(css.replace(AURORA_CSS, "")) scope, rootcls = f".nxm-p-{slug}", f":root.nxm-p-{slug}-root" hoisted, rules = scope_css(css, scope, rootcls) extra = (f"\n{scope}{{{FONT_VARS}}}\n" f"{rootcls}{{--nav-h:68px;background:#060913}}\n" f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta:only-child{{grid-column:1/-1}}\n" f"{scope} .nxm-navcta{{white-space:nowrap}}\n" f"{scope} .nv-sheet-f .nxm-navcta{{height:48px;justify-content:center;font-size:1rem}}\n" f"@media (max-width:1080px){{{scope} .nv-act>.nxm-navcta{{display:none}}}}\n") css_out = ("/* GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py from the design package — do not edit. */\n" + "\n".join(hoisted) + "\n" + "\n".join(rules) + extra) # Markup: everything between and the page script. js_at = rest.rfind("", js).group(1) assert AURORA_JS in js, "aurora.built.js not found verbatim" js = js.replace(AURORA_JS, "") js = js.replace("https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js", "/nxm/three.min.js") js = relink(js) for old, new in FIXES.get(slug, []): js = js.replace(old, new) js = js_buttons(js) if wire and hasattr(wire, "js"): js = "var __NXM = JSON.parse((document.getElementById('nxm-data') || {}).textContent || 'null');\n" + wire.js(js) assert "cdnjs" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in js and "claude.ai/artifact" not in body stale = audit(slug, body, js, getattr(wire, "ALLOW", set()) if wire else set()) STATUS[slug] = ("wired" if wire else "NOT WIRED") + (f", stale {stale}" if stale else "") d = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{slug}"; os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True) open(f"{d}/page.css", "w").write(css_out) open(f"{d}/content.ts", "w").write( "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. Trusted, static markup\n" "// from the owner's own design package (never user input).\n" f"export const TITLE = {json.dumps(title)};\n" f"export const DESCRIPTION = {json.dumps(desc)};\n" f"export const BODY_HTML = {json.dumps(body)};\n") open(f"{d}/script.ts", "w").write( "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. The page's own script.\n" f"export const PAGE_SCRIPT = {json.dumps(js)};\n") route = ROUTES[slug] loader = wire is not None and os.path.exists(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts") assert wire is None or loader, f"{slug}: wire module without app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts" has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read() for r, fixed in routes_for(slug): if ("[" in r or fixed) and not has_meta: STATUS[slug] = STATUS.get(slug, "") + f" (route {r} not written: template needs its loader)" continue write_route(slug, r, fixed, loader) print(f"{slug:36} {BASE}{route if route != '/' else ''} css {len(css_out)//1024}KB body {len(body)//1024}KB " f"js {len(js)//1024}KB buttons {btns} reviews {nrev}") return slug # ── routes ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── # A page is a TEMPLATE when its route has [params] (e.g. /mods/[family]/[slug]) # or when tools/nxm/routes/.json fans it out to many fixed routes # (e.g. the game template -> /rust-server-hosting {family: "rust"}, ...). # Loaders get the params: load(p) / meta(p). def routes_for(slug): f = f"{os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))}/routes/{slug}.json" if os.path.exists(f): return [(e["route"], e.get("params", {})) for e in json.load(open(f))] return [(ROUTES[slug], {})] def write_route(slug, route, fixed, loader): """One route file. Every route passes its [params], fixed template params and ?query (search, pagination, ?topic= deep links…) into the loader as one map; the concrete path (/mods/[family]/[slug] -> /mods/minecraft/lithium) is used for canonical and breadcrumbs.""" rd = f"{ROOT}/app/nxm{route}"; os.makedirs(rd, exist_ok=True) rel = os.path.relpath(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm", rd) pc = PARTICLES.get(slug) particles = f' particles={{{{ from: "{pc[0]}", to: "{pc[1]}" }}}}' if pc else "" has_meta = loader and "export async function meta" in open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_data/{slug}.ts").read() dyn = "[" in route assert not (dyn or fixed) or has_meta, f"{slug}: template routes need a loader with meta(p) for SEO" path_expr = ("`" + re.sub(r"\[(\w+)\]", r"${p.\1}", route) + "`") if dyn else json.dumps(route) if loader: imp = (f'import {{ load{", meta" if has_meta else ""} }} from "{rel}/_data/{slug}";\n' f'import type {{ NxmLoad }} from "{rel}/_data/lib";\n' f'import {{ nxmParams }} from "{rel}/_data/params";\n') ptype = "{ params: Promise>; searchParams: Promise> }" getp = f"const p = await nxmParams(params, searchParams, {json.dumps(fixed)});" metacall = f"nxmMetadata({path_expr}, await meta(p))" if has_meta else f"nxmMetadata({path_expr})" body = f"""export async function generateMetadata({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}): Promise {{ {getp} return {metacall}; }} export default async function Page({{ params, searchParams }}: {ptype}) {{ {getp} const d: NxmLoad = await load(p); return ; }}""" else: imp = "" body = f"""export async function generateMetadata(): Promise {{ return nxmMetadata({path_expr}); }} export default async function Page() {{ return ; }}""" open(f"{rd}/page.tsx", "w").write(f"""// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit. import type {{ Metadata }} from "next"; import {{ NxmPage }} from "{rel}/_components/NxmPage"; import {{ nxmMetadata }} from "{rel}/_seo/meta"; import * as C from "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/content"; {imp}import "{rel}/_pages/{slug}/page.css"; export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"; {body} """) if __name__ == "__main__": slugs = sys.argv[1:] or [s for s in ROUTES if s != "home"] for s in slugs: port(s) # the client runtime imports each page's script by slug keys = sorted(os.listdir(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages")) open(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/scripts.ts", "w").write( "// GENERATED by tools/nxm/port_pages.py — do not edit.\n" "// Each page's script is its own chunk, loaded only on that page.\n" "export const SCRIPTS: Record Promise<{ PAGE_SCRIPT: string }>> = {\n" + "".join(f' {json.dumps(k)}: () => import("./{k}/script"),\n' for k in keys if os.path.isdir(f"{ROOT}/app/nxm/_pages/{k}")) + "};\n") print("\nreal-data audit (launch needs every page 'wired' with no stale prices):") for k, v in STATUS.items(): print(f" {k:36} {v}") print("assets:", len(os.listdir(ASSET_DIR)), "files,", sum(os.path.getsize(f"{ASSET_DIR}/{f}") for f in os.listdir(ASSET_DIR)) // 1024 // 1024, "MB") """Shared transforms for porting the design package into app/nxm. Used by port_pages.py (every inner page) and port_home.py (links only). Each transform applies one of the owner's identity decisions (/root/nxeon-marketing-v1/IDENTITY-SPEC.md) to the package's own markup/CSS/JS. For Plutonium I'll skip custom art and use the archetype instead. I'm working out game detection by matching tags and titles against family keys, slugified display names, and hero slugs—checking cases like Left 4 Dead 2, TF2, Vintage Story, and Don't Starve Together to confirm the matching logic holds up.

I want to restrict title-based matching to avoid false positives, like "Rust" matching "trust" or "Eco" matching partial words, so I'm limiting game-art detection to tag matches or title matches only within Gaming category posts.

For posts without a detected game (like plutonium families or generic guides), I'll fall back to design archetypes like terminal, shield, or route based on topic keywords—checking for hero file existence via fs.existsSync, and mapping DNS-related terms to a route archetype and security terms to shield.

I'm working out the remaining archetype rules: vault for password/secrets content, flow for proxy/networking topics, stack for install/setup guides, chart for comparison/best-of posts, and terminal as the default for command-line tutorials. Game art takes top precedence in the ordering when a match exists.

I'm reconsidering an edge case: a "Vaultwarden behind nginx" setup should probably classify as flow rather than vault, so I need to check for reverse-proxy/nginx keywords before password-related ones, finalizing the precedence as chart, route, then flow.

Testing against sample titles like the firewall example (shield) and a malware-scanning post, I'm debating whether command-heavy titles (scan, check, tune, logs) should route to terminal ahead of shield, but I want to avoid overcomplicating the rules.

Looking at vault vs stack conflicts, I notice the distinguishing factor: posts about self-hosting Vaultwarden with docker/container/compose tags should map to stack, while plain password-manager posts without those tags map to vault.

Now I'm working out a priority ordering across categories—chart, route, flow(proxy), stack, vault, terminal, shield, flow(networking)—then trying to place an Nginx SSL setup post, torn between whether shield (security/SSL) or terminal (setup commands) should take precedence.

I'm deciding certbot/Let's Encrypt should map to terminal only when the post body actually contains commands, treating the design examples as illustrative rather than strict rules, and prioritizing sensible automatic categorization over exact matches. Now I'm defining color palettes per category: Security, Self-hosting, Web, Networking, WordPress, each with their own gradient pairs.

For real categories like Gaming, Networking, Tutorials, Security, VPS, and Domains, I'm working out palette assignments—giving VPS and Domains distinct but related hues to Networking, Gaming a magenta/violet aurora pair, and setting up a deterministic fallback scheme (hashing category names onto a list of aurora color pairs) for any unknown categories. content.content:
When a service "isn't reachable," the culprit is almost always a **port**. A port is a numbered doorway on a server — 22 for SSH, 80 for HTTP, 443 for HTTPS, 3306 for MySQL. If the door is closed or blocked, the service behind it might be running perfectly and still be invisible to the outside world. Here's how to test a port and fix it when it's shut.

## Open, closed, filtered — the three outcomes

A port check has three possible results, and knowing the difference saves hours:

- **Open** — something is listening and accepting connections. Good.
- **Closed** — the port is reachable but nothing is listening. The server refuses the connection (you'll often see "connection refused").
- **Filtered** — a firewall is silently dropping your packets, so you get no answer at all (the connection "times out"). This is the most confusing case because the service may be running fine behind the firewall.

Timeout vs refused is the single most useful signal: **refused** means you reached the machine but no service answered; **timeout** usually means a firewall ate the request.

## Checking a port from your own machine

On macOS or Linux, `nc` (netcat) is the quickest test:

```
nc -zv example.com 443
```

`-z` just scans without sending data; `-v` prints the result. You'll see "succeeded" for open or an error otherwise.

Prefer `nmap` for detail:

```
nmap -p 22,80,443 example.com
```

On Windows PowerShell:

```
Test-NetConnection example.com -Port 443
```

To see what's listening **on the server itself**, log in and run:

```
sudo ss -tulpn
```

This lists every listening port and the process behind it — the fastest way to confirm your service is actually bound.

## The catch: checking from the internet, not just locally

A port can be open on the server yet blocked before it reaches the internet. If you test from the same machine (or the same network), you're not seeing what the outside world sees. That's why an **external port checker** matters — it connects from a remote host, exactly like a real visitor would, and tells you whether the port is truly reachable across the public internet.

## What to do when a port is closed or filtered

Work through it from the inside out:

**1. Is the service running?**

```
sudo systemctl status nginx
sudo ss -tulpn | grep :443
```

If nothing is listening on the port, start or fix the service first — no firewall change will help.

**2. Is it bound to the right address?**

A service bound to `127.0.0.1` only accepts local connections. To be reachable externally it must listen on `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) or the server's public IP. Check the app's config for a `bind` or `listen` directive.

**3. Is the host firewall blocking it?**

On Ubuntu/Debian with UFW:

```
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp
sudo ufw status
```

With nftables or iptables, confirm there's an accept rule for the port.

**4. Is there a firewall in front of the server?**

Many cloud providers put a network firewall or security group ahead of the VM. If the host firewall allows the port but it's still filtered, this is usually why. On Nxeon your VPS has its own public IP and you control the firewall directly, so there's no hidden layer second-guessing your rules — what you allow is what's open.

**5. Right protocol?**

How to Self-Host Vaultwarden Behind an Nginx Reverse Proxy

Already run Nginx? Here’s how to put Vaultwarden behind it properly: real config, Let’s Encrypt TLS, WebSocket support and the security headers that matter.

NXNxeon editorialStraight-talking guides from the team that runs the serversAugust 4, 20265 min read
On this page
  1. Why the reverse proxy matters here
  2. Run Vaultwarden bound to localhost
  3. Get a certificate
  4. The Nginx site config
  5. Verify sync works
  6. Lock it down
  7. Harden and test the setup
  8. Nginx or Caddy, and where this fits
  9. Hosting other apps on the same Nginx
  10. FAQ

FAQ

Why does Vaultwarden need WebSocket proxying in Nginx?

Vaultwarden uses a WebSocket for real-time sync notifications. Without the Upgrade and Connection headers, the vault still works but changes won’t push live to other devices.

Nginx or Caddy for Vaultwarden?

Both are fine. Caddy handles TLS automatically with less config; Nginx gives you fine-grained control and suits servers already running it. This guide is for the Nginx camp.

Do I still need Certbot renewals?

Certbot sets up automatic renewal via a systemd timer. Confirm it with sudo certbot renew --dry-run so your certificate never lapses.

Should Vaultwarden be exposed directly?

No. Bind it to 127.0.0.1 as shown so only Nginx can reach it; never publish the container port to the public internet.

Run a hardened, Nginx-fronted vault on a secure NVMe VPS with full root access. See more on the security page.

I'll also standardize "Read more →" across all cards, including the featured one, since the live site is inconsistent about showing it while the design omits it entirely—adding it uniformly fixes that gap.

Now I'm sketching a cover-image system: a type for picking the relevant blog post fields, a Cover type that's either a real image or a generated SVG with architecture/logo/palette info, a function that decides which cover to use for a post, and a helper that renders the cover as HTML.

I'm deciding the hero jpg is fine to use directly even with varying aspect ratios, skipping poster art, and replicating a nice touch from the design hub where repeated game art gets an "alt" class with a scale transform so duplicate cards don't look identical.

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

## Safety rules

- NEVER touch VMIDs 9000–9999 (templates) except to add new templates.
- Staging and production share the Proxmox node but never overlap: staging only ever allocates IPs .50–.99 and ports 30000–30999. Never point staging pools at production ranges.

- Never `qm destroy` a VM that has a `Server` row — always go through a DELETE job.
- Never `pkill -f` by pattern on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit instead (a pattern match has restarted live production before).
- Do not commit `.env`. Do not print the Proxmox token into logs or docs.
- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

/** Curated popular TLDs with indicative starting prices (USD/yr). Static — live
 *  per-domain pricing comes from a search. Labelled "from". Plain module so it
 *  can be imported by both server components and the client DomainChecker.
 *
 *  Order matters: .com/.net/.org lead (what people type and trust first), then a
 *  broad set of gTLDs and ccTLDs. The exact-search endpoint (app/api/domains/check)
 *  fans a searched name across `SEARCH_TLDS` (derived from this list) in ONE
 *  batched registrar call, so a name is checked against ~two dozen extensions —
 *  not a hardcoded handful. The prices here are indicative "from" rates for the
 *  static catalog display only; a search always shows the registrar's real price. */

index 8c32c26fb7..c1792557ed 100644
--- a/tools/nxm/nxmlib.py
+++ b/tools/nxm/nxmlib.py
@@ -43,6 +43,8 @@ ROUTES = {

import net from "node:net";

/**
 * Dependency-free, in-memory sliding-window rate limiter.
 *
 * Suitable for single-process app-level throttling (login attempts, etc).
 * State lives in a module-level Map; on a horizontally-scaled deployment each
 * instance limits independently — acceptable for auth-abuse mitigation. A
 * background sweep prunes empty buckets so the Map does not grow unbounded.
 */

type Bucket = number[]; // sorted-ish list of hit timestamps (ms)

const buckets = new Map<string, Bucket>();

// Persist the Map across HMR / route reloads in dev.
const globalForRl = globalThis as unknown as { __nxeonRateLimit?: Map<string, Bucket> };
const store: Map<string, Bucket> = globalForRl.__nxeonRateLimit ?? buckets;
if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") globalForRl.__nxeonRateLimit = store;

export type RateLimitOptions = { max: number; windowMs: number };
export type RateLimitResult = { ok: boolean; retryAfterSec: number; remaining: number };

/**
 * The widest window any caller has ever asked for.
 *
 * The sweep below used a HARDCODED 15-minute horizon while callers pass windows
 * far longer than that — `RESEND_LIMIT` in lib/email-verification.ts is an hour,
 * as are the mail-send, calendar-mutation, org-invite and wallet-top-up limits.
 * A bucket whose last hit was 16 minutes ago was therefore DELETED, and deleting
 * a bucket resets its counter: "5 verification emails per hour" was really "5
 * per 15 minutes, forever", and "60 outbound mails per hour" was 60 per quarter
 * hour. The limiter silently enforced a limit nobody had chosen, and the longer
 * the window a caller asked for, the less of it was honoured.
 *
 * Tracking the real maximum keeps the sweep's only job — bounding the Map — from
 * quietly becoming a policy decision. It only ever grows, so it can never evict a
 * bucket that some caller still considers live.
 */
let widestWindowMs = 15 * 60 * 1000;

## Blog hub, article template, cover system and contact form: wired to real data (staging only, nothing committed)

All three slugs regenerate cleanly: `python3 tools/nxm/port_pages.py blog blog-vaultwarden-nginx contact` reports **blog / blog-vaultwarden-nginx / contact: wired**, with no stale values. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` passes. `/nxm/blog/[slug]` is now generated for every post, and an unknown slug returns 404.

### Files (all mine; nothing shared was edited)
- `tools/nxm/wire/blog.py`, `tools/nxm/wire/blog_vaultwarden_nginx.py`, `tools/nxm/wire/contact.py`
- `app/nxm/_data/blog.ts`: hub loader and `meta`.
- `app/nxm/_data/blog-vaultwarden-nginx.ts`: article `load` and `meta`.
- `app/nxm/_data/blog-article.ts`: turns renderArticle's HTML into the design's markup.
- `app/nxm/_data/blog-covers.ts`: the cover system.
- `app/nxm/_data/blog-product.ts`: real "from" prices.
